input: Write a professional bio for my author website

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Author bios vary widely in length — a 50-word blurb serves a completely different purpose than a 300-word narrative, and the structure changes accordingly.
The bio needs to reflect the author's actual background: genres written, publications, credentials, awards, or other career highlights that establish credibility.
The genre and audience of the author's work shapes the tone and content — a literary fiction writer's bio reads very differently from a business book author's or a romance novelist's.
Bio tone can range from formal third-person professional to warm and conversational first-person; the author's preference fundamentally changes how it is written.
Knowing what the bio must achieve — build trust, attract readers, appeal to agents/publishers, or sell books — determines what to emphasise and what to leave out.
Whether this replaces an existing bio or is written from scratch affects the starting point; knowing if there is an old draft or raw notes to work from saves significant effort.
Some website layouts, publisher submission pages, or personal preferences impose a hard word or character limit that must be respected.

gold.taskTitle: Write a professional bio for author website
gold.taskDescription: Draft a polished, professional author biography to be published on the user's personal author website.

questions.title: How long should the finished bio be?
questions.description: Determine the target word count or length range for the bio (e.g., short blurb ~50 words, medium ~150 words, full narrative ~300+ words).

questions.title: What genre or type of books do you write?
questions.description: Identify the author's writing genre(s) and audience so the bio content and framing are relevant and credible to the right readers.

questions.title: What key credentials or career highlights should be included?
questions.description: Gather the most important facts to feature: published titles, awards, prior careers, education, media appearances, or other notable achievements.

questions.title: Should the bio be written in first or third person?
questions.description: Establish the grammatical perspective, which also signals the overall tone — third person reads more formal and traditional; first person feels more direct and personal.

questions.title: What is the primary goal this bio needs to achieve?
questions.description: Clarify the main purpose — attracting new readers, impressing industry contacts like agents or publishers, building personal brand trust, or something else — to sharpen the focus.

questions.title: Do you have an existing bio or raw notes to start from?
questions.description: Check whether there is a previous version, a rough draft, a resume snippet, or a list of facts already written that can serve as a foundation.

questions.title: Is there a strict word or character limit to stay within?
questions.description: Identify any hard constraints imposed by the website template, a publisher submission requirement, or personal preference that the final bio must not exceed.
